implemented_api_before_this_task: capability.rs::availability(id) decided from the recorded receipts alone (Rust semantic/runtime receipt, native ABI closure, commit receipt) and returned Availability { enabled, reason }
capability.rs::admit(id, kind, options, phase) — the gate a running command passes — checked availability(id) and compared option names EXACTLY
gap_found_by_this_task: Nothing in the descriptor could say what the command needs from the session, so an unavailable command could only be refused after it started, and admit() had no session state at all.

admit() compared option names case-sensitively while the descriptor declares them without case (Operation::option), so an option the descriptor accepts (`bothsides` for `BothSides`) was refused by the gate: the two readers of one name disagreed.

admit_with() is the gate that takes the real session context; admit() keeps its signature and delegates with an empty context, which means 'no context is claimed', so a command that needs a document is refused rather than run blind.
reuse_decision: ADAPT the 'the operation says why it cannot continue' habit of gui.rs; ADD the declared preconditions, the context-checked availability and the context-checked gate.
